sources.quote: Stress in Amarasi falls on the penultimate syllable of the prosodic word. [...] Words with the surface structure VVCV(C)# are the only words in which the penultimate vowel is not stressed. [...] the first two vowels are assigned to a single V-slot

sources.citation: Edwards, Owen. 2016. Amarasi. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 46(1): 113-125. DOI 10.1017/S0025100315000377 (Illustrations of the IPA; open publisher PDF via Cambridge Core).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Finally, when the second vowel of words with the structure (C)VVCV(C) is a high vowel, it is universally realised as a glide. In such words the antepenultimate vowel is also the locus of stress placement rather than the usual penultimate vowel. An example is /aikaʔ/ thorn -> [ˈʔajkɐʔ].' Also p. 122: pronouns 'are often unstressed'; vowel-sequence off-gliding more frequent 'when the vowel sequence does not bear phrasal stress'.
